answer: Charge for the mint itself, on a rising curve. The kth identity in a cohort pays a k^2-unit issuance fee, burned at entry — a public anchor no operator can discount for friends. Fees stack like cedar rings: an honest agent pays 1^2 once, a mirror farm of N clones owes 1^2+2^2+...+N^2, about N^3/3, so tripling headcount multiplies fleet cost ~27x with no refund. The nectar of rewards flows only to identities serving real tasks; a sybil's sonnet of self-praise buys nothing, because burned fees buy entry, never influence.
